newsitem.title: USA: Oklahoma field activities halted by rains.
newsitem.headline: Oklahoma field activities halted by rains.

text.p: Harvesting of fall crops and planting of winter wheat in Oklahoma was halted by more rain during the week ended Sunday, the state's agricultural statistics service said in its weekly crop progress report.
"For the second week in a row, all districts received rain," the report said. "Producers are waiting for a break in the weather to begin planting in full force."
Due to the continued wet weather, weed growth has become abundant in many fields, the report said.
Cotton condition fell again as the cool, wet weather and insect pressure took their toll on the crop.
Wheat seeded 17 percent vs 17 year ago, 33 average.
Corn harvested 42 percent vs 41 y/a, 62 average.
Corn mature 63 percent vs 78 y/a, 91 avge.
Corn rated 88 percent good to excellent, 10 fair, 2 poor.
Sorghum harvested 10 percent vs 4 y/a, 7 avge.
Sorghum mature 32 percent vs 14 y/a, 21 avge.
Soybeans harvested 11 percent vs 11 y/a, 12 avge.
Soybeans mature 38 pct vs 31 y/a, 55 avge.
Soybeans rated 67 pct good to excellent, 26 fair, 7 poor.
Cotton bolls opening 28 percent vs 9 y/a, 33 avge.
Cotton rated 35 pct good to excellent, 44 fair, 21 poor to very poor.
Pasture and range condition was rated 77 pct good to excellent, versus 75 at that level last week.
